1.$description: Script-readable: ArenaMenu's gap from its trigger is one and a half of this, and that gap is the offset a CDK overlay position strategy computes in JS, so no stylesheet can hold it.

2.$description: Script-readable: ArenaTooltip's gap from its trigger is the offset a CDK overlay position strategy computes in JS, so no stylesheet can hold it.

3.$description: Script-readable: ArenaOnboarding's gap below its anchor is arithmetic on a DOMRect.

4.$description: Script-readable: ArenaOnboarding's minimum gutter from either viewport edge, compared against window.innerWidth.

rhythm.$description:
Page rhythm: the air BETWEEN two components, which Arena itself never
draws. Every component is an inner box carrying no outer margin, so the space between one
and the next belongs to whoever places them, and a system that ships the grid without
naming any step on it leaves every adopter to pick their own. These are aliases of sp
rather than fresh numbers, so a rhythm step cannot drift off the 4px grid, and the three
of them are the steps ArenaGrid's gap variant had already chosen before they had names.

Deliberately not part of dz, on the same cut that separates fs from dz: dz is how dense the
CONTROLS are and re-densifies under .arena-compact, while this is how a PAGE breathes and
does not. That is why rhythm-group and dz-stack are both 12px, the way fs-sm and dz-text-md
are both 13px: same length, different question.

group.$description: Inside one group of related things: a label and its field, a card's own stacked children, a row of chips. Both sides read as one unit.

component.$description: Between two peer components: a card and the next card, a chart and the table under it. Both sides are separate things standing on the same footing.

section.$description: Between two sections of a page. The two sides answer different questions, and this gap is what says so.

layout.$description:
Application frame. Example code, and therefore the numbers a consumer
copies. Arena draws neither of these itself: the sidebar is the console shell's
and the bar is a phone shell's, and they are declared for the same reason --z-nav
is, because the frame a consumer builds is part of the system and every one of
them otherwise invents its own number.

sidebar.$description: The width of the console shell's navigation column.

bar.$description:
The height of a fixed bottom navigation bar, the row of destinations a
phone shell puts at the foot of the screen. It is read from outside the bar as often
as inside it: the page reserves it as bottom padding so the last row is not covered,
and a stack of toasts sits above it rather than under it, so a bar whose height only
the bar knows is a number retyped in three files. The safe-area inset is NOT included:
add var(--pad-safe-bottom) to it, since a value that already carried the inset could
not be used as a plain height. Not script-readable: nothing computes a position from
it, a stylesheet holds every use, and a number bound at import time could not
re-densify.

bp.$description:
Breakpoints: SHARED VALUES READ BY JS, not media queries.
Components style themselves with inline style objects, which cannot hold a
media query, so responsive branches are JS (see UseArenaContainerWidth.ts).
These live here anyway so the thresholds stay a token, not a magic number
retyped in four components. 768px is what DAMA hardcodes.

dz.$description:
Density (H7 rev.3): comfortable by default. Data-dense surfaces read these
instead of hard-coded px so a single scope switch re-densifies rows and controls.

text-lg.$description: the largest control text: a data readout inside a chart, where the number is the content rather than a label

text.$description: control text: buttons, inputs, selects, menu items, table cells

text-md.$description: secondary control text: tag chips, pagination, secondary buttons

text-sm.$description: secondary control text: hints, validation errors, badges, legends

text-xs.$description: micro control text: field labels, shortcuts, eyebrow labels

lh.$description: glyph-tight line height: the control reset. Unlike every other dz member this is unitless, so it carries its own $type override: a line height is a number, not a dimension, the same distinction that puts lh in typography.json to begin with. Used wherever a box must be exactly its glyph (an icon inside a button, a standalone icon, an icon-only close/remove control), so the line box never throws the surrounding control out of alignment.

avatar.$description:
ArenaAvatar diameters. The first family named after a component rather
than a role, and worth stating rather than glossing: dz and icon are named for
roles. It earns its place because ArenaAvatar derives two values from its own
diameter (the initials at 0.4 and the presence dot at 0.28), and a derivation
needs something to derive from. If a second component ever wants the same
ladder, rename this for the role instead of duplicating it.

xs.$description: Script-readable, and so are its three siblings, for one reason: an reserves its box before the stylesheet arrives through the width and height attributes, which take a bare integer and cannot take a custom property. So the number has to reach JavaScript or the avatar is the one image in the library whose space is not held. Reading it here rather than restating it in each layer is what keeps the reserved box and the drawn box the same number.

logo.$description:
Brand lock-up scale: the mark's slot and the wordmark's size, in
four steps. These are tokens rather than an exemption for one reason: ArenaAppLogo
takes the mark and the name from its consumer, so once they are the consumer's
brand these numbers stop being Dravensoft's identity and become the system's
answer to 'how big is a small logo'. A scale is a scale, and Arena's scales are
tokens.

A fixed repertoire rather than one mark-to-text ratio, because no single ratio
is right at every step: a small lock-up needs proportionally larger text to stay
legible, and one constant across the scale would either shrink the small
wordmark below reading size or inflate the large one. The eight numbers are
declared and the proportions that fall out (0.57, 0.60, 0.63, 0.63) are a
consequence rather than a rule.

No number here was invented. sm and md are exactly what the console's Shell and
LoginScreen rendered before they migrated; lg and xl are the approved brand
manual's Primary · horizontal and its large specimen.

mark-sm.$description: beside a product name in an application frame

mark-xl.$description: the hero case: the lock-up is the only thing on the screen

text-sm.$description: the wordmark beside mark-sm: the smallest that still reads as a name rather than a label

text-md.$description: the wordmark beside mark-md, in a signed-out panel

text-lg.$description: the wordmark beside mark-lg, in the manual's Primary · horizontal

text-xl.$description: the wordmark beside mark-xl, at hero size
